title: Good: yencoding-multi Assembler overlap detection is O(log n) per part via BTreeMap
description: yencoding-multi/src/assembler.rs: overlap detection uses a BTreeMap<u64, u64> (start → end of covered interval). On each add_part() call, the code uses .range(..=begin_0).next_back() and .range(begin_0..).next() to find the immediate predecessor and successor intervals in O(log n) time. This is the correct data structure for an interval coverage problem: a Vec would require O(n) scan and sort maintenance. The missing_ranges() walk is also O(n) in the number of parts, not O(total_size). Worth defending: a reviewer might suggest 'just use a Vec<bool>' which would be O(total_size) in space and time.
